subject: bumblebee
title: Bumblebees Roll Tiny Balls for No Reward. One Did It 117 Times

scenes.text: Scientists gave bumblebees tiny balls. Nobody taught them what to do with them.
The balls sat beside the path to the food. Rolling them earned nothing at all.
The bees rolled them anyway, again and again. One bee rolled balls 117 times.
Young bees rolled the most, and males rolled for longer than females.
Researchers in London called it the first evidence that an insect plays.
No food, no reward. Just a bee, having fun.

description:
Bumblebees roll balls just for fun, according to a 2022 Queen Mary University of London study.
The balls were placed beside the route to food and rolling them earned nothing, yet bees rolled them repeatedly: individual bees rolled balls between 1 and 117 times. Younger bees rolled more than older ones, and males rolled for longer than females.
What other animal do you think plays just for fun?
first_comment: One bee rolled a ball 117 times for nothing. What do you do just for fun?
